metadata.case_name: WONG SIN LAM v. KUEN FUNG CONSTRUCTION LTD. AND OTHERS

source: severe brain injuries he suffered on that day on site in March 1998.

injuries.description: compound fracture of the left temporo-parietal skull vault
source: He suffered a compound fracture of the left temporo-parietal skull vault and a thick left temporal extradural haematoma.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of vault of skull, unspecified

source: He suffered a compound fracture of the left temporo-parietal skull vault and a thick left temporal extradural haematoma.

injuries.description: stable fracture of C2 in the cervical spine
source: In addition to the cerebral injuries, he had also suffered a stable fracture of C2 in the cervical spine, and his intensive care stay was further complicated by pneumonia, aspiration and sepsis.

injuries.description: ventriculitis, a bacterial infection of the cerebral ventricles
source: ventriculitis, a bacterial infection of the cerebral ventricles, developed at the site of the intraventricular catheter and required treatment by antibiotics.

injuries.description: subglottic stenosis secondary to the plaintiff's tracheostomy
source: reports ... speak to throat problems consequent upon the subglottic stenosis secondary to the plaintiff's tracheostomy shortly after the accident.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the neck

manifestations.description: has been rendered a mild mental defective (IQ estimated by Professor Lee at 69, and by Dr Chan at 61)
impairment of intellectual capacity; both long term and short term learning and memory functions are impaired
ability to monitor and to regulate his thought and behaviour is impaired, resulting in irritability, impulsivity, rigidity, egocentricity and lack of volition
uncontrolled violent and vulgar behaviour, lewd behaviour, aggression and unprovoked violence
mild degree of difficulty of bladder control
a 17% risk of developing epilepsy (as identified by Dr Kan; defence accepted risk not more than 5% in submission)
lost totally his working or earning capacity
ventriculitis (bacterial infection of the cerebral ventricles) developed at the site of the intraventricular catheter
swallowing problem if food is eaten fast
requires a variety of medicines for the rest of his life and continuous lifetime monitoring by a psychiatrist

treatments_received.treatment: emergency left parietal craniectomy to evacuate the blood clot
source: he was transferred to Prince of Wales Hospital for an emergency left parietal craniectomy necessary to evacuate the blood clot.

treatments_received.treatment: insertion of a left frontal ventricular catheter
source: A left frontal ventricular catheter was inserted, and he was transferred to the ICU.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Creation of ventriculoperitoneal shunt or subcutaneous cerebrospinal fluid reservoir

source: A tracheostomy was performed on 19 March 1998, and thereafter ventriculitis ... developed at the site of the intraventricular catheter and required treatment by antibiotics.
ventriculitis, a bacterial infection of the cerebral ventricles, developed at the site of the intraventricular catheter and required treatment by antibiotics.
after being taken off a ventilator he was able to be transferred to a neurosurgical ward, and on 30 March 1998 was transferred to a Cheshire Home for further rehabilitation

treatments_received.treatment: psychiatric inpatient management and admissions (Prince of Wales Psychiatric Ward; Shatin Hospital; Castle Peak Hospital)
source: Soon after returning to hospital, Mr Wong was admitted to the Prince of Wales Psychiatric Ward for management of his psychiatric problems

on 12 March 1999 Mr Wong was confined to Castle Peak Hospital under compulsory order ... and he remained there as an inmate until 7 January 2000 when he was transferred back to Psychiatry at Shatin Hospital.
he had briefly to return to Prince of Wales on 23 April 1998 for removal of the tracheostomy tube

treatments_received.treatment: monthly outpatient psychiatric treatment at the Lee Ka Shing Psychiatric Clinic
source: he has been receiving psychiatric treatment free of charge once a month at the Lee Ka Shing Psychiatric Clinic

there was agreement amongst all the experts that Mr Wong's impairments are permanent, and it further is accepted that Mr Wong will require to take a variety of medicines, in all probability similar to his present extensive drug regime, for the rest of his life

treatments_future.treatment: continuous lifetime monitoring by a psychiatrist
source: he will require continuous lifetime monitoring by a psychiatrist who will adjust appropriately the types and dosages of the various medicines required to control his condition

losses.description: has been rendered a mild mental defective (IQ estimated at 69 and 61); impairment of intellectual capacity and both long term and short term learning and memory functions are impaired
has been rendered an egocentric, obstinate and selfish child; irritability, impulsivity, rigidity, egocentricity and lack of volition
dependent upon the care of his wife and elder daughter for all manner of requirements of daily life

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: dependent for organizing his clothes, combing his hair and running the bath water to the provision of meals
has lost totally his working or earning capacity
destruction of a fulfilling and contented family life

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
